matchupAnalysis: Tuivasa 54.2%, and this is the card's sharpest split between the model's two layers. The hand-tuned layer makes Despaigne a clear favourite (Tuivasa just 23.4%); the GBM flips it to 55.4% Tuivasa, and the final number follows the GBM. Elo sides with Tuivasa by 159 points (1497 to 1339), but his 1497 is the residue of six straight losses, the last four being Marcin Tybura (a round-one submission) and three decisions to Jairzinho Rozenstruik, Tallison Teixeira and Louie Sutherland. Despaigne's 1339 comes from only three UFC bouts (1-2).

The hand-tuned case for Despaigne is physical. At 6'7" he has a 213.4cm reach to Tuivasa's 190.5cm (reach +2.23 to -0.98), a decision edge of -1.16 in his favour, and the fight's best KO threat (1.50; Tuivasa's is -0.04). Tuivasa's composites are poor outside his punch: output -0.83, grappling -0.79, chin -0.82 with a 0.66 chin-damage modifier. What pulls the GBM the other way is how little, and how long ago, Despaigne has shown anything. He has 30 minutes of UFC evidence (trust 0.43), is 38.0 (age factor 0.85), and hasn't fought since October 2024: 696 days, the only layoff on the card long enough to draw a penalty (layoff factor 0.91). His two UFC losses were both decisions, after a first-round knockout of Josh Parisian.

Both routes run through a knockout. Tuivasa wins 34.0% by KO (seven of his eight UFC wins came that way), Despaigne 22.1%. Only 34.9% go the distance and 37.7% end in round one. The blended O/U has Over 1.5 at 53.3% and Over 2.5 at 38.9%. Despaigne's record was refreshed to 6-2 before this run.

synopsis.body: A weak one, and the least settled pick on the card. The hand-tuned layer likes Despaigne's enormous reach and KO threat; the GBM, which drives the final number, discounts a 38-year-old coming off nearly two years out with 30 UFC minutes to his name. Tuivasa 54.2%, despite six straight losses. Expect it to be short: nearly two-thirds of simulations end inside the distance.

Steveson is close to a blank page for the model. One UFC fight, a first-round knockout of Elisha Ellison in 2.5 minutes, puts his trust at 0.04 and his decision trust at 0.00, so every composite sits at the heavyweight mean (grappling -0.01, wrestling defence +0.01). His Olympic freestyle wrestling pedigree is invisible to the data. The pre-UFC features carry his 3-0 regional record, all knockouts; that row was missing until this run and was scraped from Sherdog. His real measurements were also missing: ufcstats now lists 5'11" and a 74-inch reach, which replaced a 180cm default (reach -2.86 to -1.46) and was worth about 1.4pp to him. He still gives up 7.6cm of reach to the 6'3" Sharaf.

The KO threat gap is 1.19 to 0.10 and the decision edge +1.04. Steveson wins 47.6% by knockout, 24.3% by decision and 6.6% by submission. Sharaf's 21.6% is split across KO (8.9%), decision (8.2%) and submission (4.5%). The sim finishes 67.6% of fights, 38.8% in round one. The blended O/U has Over 1.5 at 51.9% and Over 2.5 at 36.8%. synopsis.body: The model knows almost nothing about Steveson and quite a lot about Sharaf: two knockout losses in two UFC fights and a chin that reads -1.13. That is enough for 78.4%, with close to half of all outcomes a Steveson knockout. The wrestling that defines Steveson isn't in the numbers at all, so if anything the model is flying blind on his best weapon.

matchupAnalysis: Yoo 52.6%, the closest fight on the card, and the model's layers point in opposite directions. The GBM leans Yoo (54.9%), the hand-tuned layer Aswell (56.0%), and the final number follows the GBM. Elo is Yoo's by 201 points (1605 to 1404), but it is thin on both sides. Yoo's featherweight rating rests on a single bout, a first-round KO of Jeka Saragih (his loss to Daniel Santos was at catchweight). Aswell's 1404 reflects a 1-4 UFC run.

Aswell's four UFC losses were all decisions, and his one win was a first-round knockout of Lucas Almeida. His profile says the same: power +0.83, chin +0.34, output +0.44, at a trust of 0.88 over 62 minutes. His KO threat (1.29) is the fight's only real one; Yoo's is 0.08. The model barely knows Yoo: two UFC fights, 5.8 minutes, trust 0.08, so his composites sit near the prior. His chin reads -0.58 after the Santos knockout, and he has been out 346 days. He has 5.1cm more reach (180.3 to 175.3).

Both men's pre-UFC rows were 0-0 placeholders before this run. They were backfilled from Sherdog (Aswell 10-2, Yoo 8-0), so both fighters' pre-UFC features now reflect real records. That matters most for Yoo, whose UFC sample is almost empty. The method split mirrors the profiles: Aswell 25.9% by KO and 17.8% by decision; Yoo 24.1% decision, 16.3% KO, 12.3% submission. 42.0% go the distance, and the blended O/U has Over 1.5 at 57.7% and Over 2.5 at 45.5%.

synopsis.body: By the narrowest margin on the card (52.6%), so treat it as close to a pass. Aswell has the knockout power and 62 minutes of UFC evidence, but a 1-4 record. Yoo has an unbeaten regional career and almost no UFC sample. If Aswell lands, he is the likelier finisher; if not, it is a close decision either way.
